text:
maya: Heads up — after landing the Rust SDK retry-refactor, a couple of our webhook sample customers in staging are seeing duplicates when receivers return 429 with a Retry-After HTTP-date. Small rate (~0.3%) but reproducible.
ci-bot: deploy: rust-sdk@0.9.0 promoted to staging (2026-03-28T09:12:01Z) :rocket:
kevin: Do we have a concrete trace? important: is the SDK mis-parsing the HTTP-date into a negative duration because of clock skew/parse rounding?
maya: Example sanitized trace:
```
POST /callback -> 429
Headers: Retry-After: Sun, 28 Mar 2026 09:15:00 GMT
Client retry immediately -> 200 (duplicate delivered)
```
oliver: From quick glance at the new middleware, it attempts to parse Retry-After as seconds then falls back to DateTime::parse_from_rfc2822 and does wait = parsed - now. If parse yields a time that is <= now (due to small clock skew) we were clamping to 0 but then the jitter function sometimes returns negative micro-adjustment in our impl (bug), so net wait became negative and we scheduled immediate retry.
sara: Also the sample-apps omitted any idempotency token on outgoing webhooks. They assumed receivers dedup. With an aggressive immediate retry that's not safe.
kevin: Action items I propose: 1) Fix Rust jitter to always add [0, +jitter] (non-negative). 2) Update parse fallback to treat past or equal dates as a minimal positive wait (e.g., 1s) instead of 0 to avoid race. 3) Attach X-Redwood-Webhook-Id (uuid4) by default from SDK sample helpers; samples must opt-out explicitly. 4) Add telemetry metric webhook_duplicate_count and emit when we detect same payload id delivered twice within window.
maya: Agreed. Also add a small opt-in compatibility flag `legacy_retry_behavior` default false so we can quickly revert to old behavior if something else regresses.
oliver: Quick Rust pseudo:
```
let ra = headers.get("retry-after");
let wait = if ra.chars().all(|c| c.is_digit(10)) {
  Duration::from_secs(ra.parse::<u64>()?)
} else if let Ok(t) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc2822(ra) {
  let delta = t.with_timezone(&Utc) - Utc::now();
  if delta.num_seconds() <= 0 { Duration::from_secs(1) } else { Duration::from_std(delta.to_std()?)? }
} else { default_backoff };
let wait = wait + Duration::from_millis(rand::thread_rng().gen_range(0..jitter_ms));
sleep(wait).await;
```
kevin: For parity: C# had a subtle bug where Retry-After header parsing honored HTTP-date but used local time without normalizing to UTC, causing off-by-hours in weird infra. Let's add a small cross-SDK test harness that returns both delta-seconds and RFC1123 date strings and asserts clients wait roughly the right amount.
sara: CI: I'll add a sample lint rule that fails if a sample webhook sender doesn't include X-Redwood-Webhook-Id unless explicitly configured. Also add an integration job `samples/webhook-replay` that simulates 429 numeric/date combos.
maya: Telemetry + alerts: emit webhook_duplicate_detected and create a simple dashboard with staging/prod split. Alert if duplicate rate > 0.2% in prod or >0.05% in staging.
oliver: I'll open a small Rust PR with the jitter clamp, date fallback minimal-wait, and unit tests for numeric/date/expired-date cases. I'll also add an optional config toggle `attach_webhook_id` default true.
kevin: I'll add cross-sdk harness and a C# patch to normalize times to UTC. Also add unit tests for RFC1123 parsing.
sara: ETA: PRs today EOD, CI lint and sample test tomorrow, staging smoke after lunch.
maya: Good. Add a blurb in release notes about "Fix: Retry-After parsing + safer jitter to reduce duplicate webhook deliveries; sample apps now attach idempotency header by default." Also include migration note for self-hosted SDK users.
kevin: One more quick thought: we should document the exact idempotency contract in devex (header name, recommended TTL, semantics) so receivers can implement dedupe windows consistently. I'll draft that doc and link it in the sample README.
maya: Thanks team :thumbsup: Action items: oliver -> Rust PR + tests, kevin -> C# + harness, sara -> CI lint + samples job, maya -> release note + doc. Keep updates here.
